text:
Landed. Two opaque types (DesignId[Tag], OneBasedIndex[Tag]), two sealed abstract companions (IdCompanion[Tag](kind), IndexCompanion[Tag](kind)), and phantom tags in IdTag/IndexTag. Each concrete type is two lines:

  type ColumnId = DesignId[IdTag.Column]
  object ColumnId extends IdCompanion[IdTag.Column]("column")

Distinctness is preserved: DesignId[IdTag.Column] and DesignId[IdTag.Term] are different types and the compiler rejects passing one for the other.

Correction to the estimate in this bead: ~130 lines did not become ~30. The 129 lines of repetition became 20 lines of concrete types, but the shared definitions, tags, and docs replacing them are ~70 lines, so DesignTypes.scala went 190 -> 174 overall — and that file also gained two DesignError cases and the parsing contract in prose along the way. The property that mattered holds: ten copies of one definition are now one definition used ten times.

Sequencing held — this ran after the phase 1 round-trip fix, so the shared definition encodes preserve-on-parse rather than entrenching sanitize-on-parse.

design 157 tests, JVM+JS green.
